newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda posts modest interim profit under Wallace.
newsitem.headline: Mazda posts modest interim profit under Wallace.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp posted a modest half-year profit on Friday in its first earnings results since Ford's Henry Wallace slipped into the driver's seat.

After a string of first-half losses, Mazda announced on Friday that it managed a parent current profit of 2.08 billion yen ($18.7 million) for the six months to the end of September, a boost for its new president, the first foreigner to head a major Japanese firm.

Wallace, a Briton, took the wheel at Japan's fifth-largest car maker in June, soon after Ford Motor Co raised its holding in the firm to a one-third stake from the previous 25 percent, giving it management control.

Mazda, whose range of models has failed to excite Japanese customers at a time when its competitors are coming up with a host of popular new models, had posted first-half losses for three straight years. It had forecast nil profit for the period.
The interim result was partly due to sales of securities holdings. Current profit is pre-tax and includes losses or gains on non-operating activities, such as sales of stocks.

Despite the past series of first-half losses, Mazda last year posted a full-year current profit of 1.23 billion yen ($11.0 million) -- the first such annual profit in three years -- thanks to sales of securities and painful cost-cutting.

Mazda said it would enjoy a profit of 11 billion yen ($99.0 million) this fiscal year, almost nine times higher than last year, but the figure was still lower than its May estimate of 25 billion yen ($225 million).

Analysts said the full-year figure would be helped by the weaker yen, which makes Japanese exports more competitive abroad. A dollar rise by one yen translates into 3 billion yen ($27.0 million) of annual profits for Mazda, analysts said. The dollar stood at around 111 yen on Friday, against 100 yen a year ago.
But Mazda's business environment remains tough.
On a group basis, the firm said it was likely to a suffer net loss of four billion yen ($36 million) for the full year, despite a May forecast of a net profit of 10 billion yen ($90 million).

The firm also lowered its domestic output forecast for the full year to 775,000 vehicles from a May forecast of 810,000 and its overseas production forecast to 160,000 units from a May projection of 177,000.

It lowered its domestic sales forecast to 395,000 vehicles from an earlier forecast of 440,000, but raised its forecast for exports, which account for more than half of its total vehicle sales, to 445,000 units from a May projection of 430,000. ($1=111)
